$comment: Copilot Studio feature catalog. Drives the Lab Builder wizard. Each selected feature becomes one lab chapter. learnQueries feed the Microsoft Learn MCP server; docUrls are the pages the step deriver reads for each module, and the citation fallback when a search returns nothing relevant. steps are the fallback walk-through, used whenever no procedure on those pages matches the module closely enough, which is a common path rather than a rare one. docsReviewed is the catalog-wide date the docUrls were last checked against live documentation; leave it null unless someone actually checked, because the builder quotes it when asking a human whether to build on the fallback links, and a wrong freshness date is worse than none. The builder prefers a per-feature lastVerified date over it, but no feature carries one yet (issue #42).

features.name: Create an agent
features.summary: Create a new Copilot Studio agent from a natural-language description or from a blank template.
features.whyItMatters: Everything else in Copilot Studio hangs off the agent object. Describing the agent in natural language lets the platform pre-write the name, description, and instructions, which is the fastest path from idea to working prototype.
concepts: Agents are environment-scoped: the environment you pick decides which connectors, Dataverse tables, and DLP policies apply.
The 'describe it to create it' flow generates a starting name, description, and instructions that you then refine by hand.
An unpublished agent is still fully testable in the authoring canvas, so you can iterate before anyone else sees it.
steps: Sign in to Copilot Studio and confirm the environment picker in the top-right shows your lab environment.
Select **Create**, then choose **New agent**.
Describe the agent in one or two sentences covering who it helps and what it does.
Review the generated name, description, and instructions, then refine them for your scenario.
Select **Create** to provision the agent and land on its **Overview** page.
validation: The agent appears under **Agents** in your lab environment.
The Overview page shows a name, description, and non-empty instructions.

instructions: Open the Create > New agent experience.
Show the natural-language description box with your scenario text typed in.
Open the new agent's Overview page.
Show name, description, and instructions.

learnQueries: Copilot Studio create a new agent quickstart
Copilot Studio describe it to create it agent

reuseScreenshots.caption: Copilot Studio home — agent list for the current environment

features.name: Agent instructions & persona
features.summary: Write the system instructions that define the agent's role, scope, tone, and refusal behavior.
features.whyItMatters: With generative orchestration the instructions are the primary control surface. Vague instructions produce vague agents; explicit scope and escalation rules are what make an agent safe to hand to real users.
concepts: Instructions are read on every turn, so they cost tokens — be specific but not sprawling.
Say what the agent must NOT do as clearly as what it must do; out-of-scope handling is where most pilots fail.
Name the tools and knowledge sources you expect the agent to prefer, so the orchestrator has routing hints.
steps: Open the agent and go to **Overview**, then edit **Instructions**.
State the agent's role and audience in the first line.
Add the tasks it should handle, referencing the knowledge sources or tools by name.
Add explicit out-of-scope rules and an escalation path.
Add tone and formatting guidance, then save and test in the **Test** pane.
validation: Asking an in-scope question returns a grounded, on-tone answer.
Asking an out-of-scope question produces the documented refusal or escalation, not a guess.

instructions: Show the Instructions editor with your finished instruction text.
Open the Test pane and ask an in-scope question.
Capture the grounded response.

learnQueries: Copilot Studio agent instructions best practices
Copilot Studio write effective agent instructions generative orchestration

features.name: Generative orchestration
features.summary: Turn on generative orchestration so the agent plans across topics, knowledge, and tools instead of matching one trigger phrase.
features.whyItMatters: Classic orchestration picks a single topic per turn. Generative orchestration lets the agent chain several knowledge lookups and tool calls in one turn, which is what makes multi-step business questions answerable.
concepts: Generative orchestration uses tool and topic **descriptions** for routing — descriptions are effectively prompts.
The activity map in the Test pane shows the plan the orchestrator chose, which is your primary debugging tool.
Classic orchestration is still the right choice when you need strictly deterministic, compliance-fixed dialog paths.
steps: Open **Settings** > **Generative AI** for the agent.
Set orchestration to **Generative** and save.
Ask a question that needs two sources to answer.
Open the activity map in the **Test** pane and read the plan the orchestrator produced.
Tighten any tool or topic description that was skipped or wrongly selected, then retest.
validation: A single question produces a plan that touches more than one knowledge source or tool.
The activity map shows the expected tools in the expected order.

instructions: Open Settings > Generative AI.
Show the orchestration selection.
Ask a multi-source question in the Test pane.
Expand the activity map so the plan steps are visible.

learnQueries: Copilot Studio generative orchestration
Copilot Studio orchestration activity map debugging

features.name: Model selection
features.summary: Choose the underlying model for the agent and compare quality, latency, and cost tradeoffs.
features.whyItMatters: Model choice is a per-agent lever on response quality, latency, and Copilot Credit burn. Picking the largest model for a simple FAQ agent wastes budget; picking the smallest for multi-step reasoning breaks orchestration.
concepts: Reasoning-heavy orchestration benefits from stronger models; short retrieval answers usually do not.
Latency is user-visible in voice and Teams channels, so measure it, do not assume it.
Always re-run your evaluation set after changing models — model swaps are regressions until proven otherwise.
steps: Open **Settings** > **Generative AI** and locate the model selection control.
Record the current model and run three representative prompts, noting quality and response time.
Switch to an alternate model and save.
Re-run the same three prompts and record the same measurements.
Choose the model that meets your quality bar at the lowest latency and cost, and document the decision.
validation: You have a side-by-side comparison table for at least two models.
The selected model is saved and the agent still answers all three prompts correctly.

instructions: Show the model selection control in Settings > Generative AI.

learnQueries: Copilot Studio model selection agent
Copilot Studio choose AI model for agent

features.name: Publish the agent
features.summary: Publish the agent so channel changes take effect for real users.
features.whyItMatters: Authoring changes are invisible to published channels until you publish. Almost every 'my change didn't work' support case starts here.
concepts: Publishing is per-agent and pushes the current authoring state to every connected channel at once.
The Test pane always runs the latest authoring state, which is why it can disagree with Teams.
In managed environments, publishing may be gated by solution and pipeline policy.
steps: Select **Publish** in the agent command bar.
Review the summary of what will be published and confirm.
Wait for the publish confirmation banner.
Open a published channel and confirm your latest change is live.
validation: The agent shows a recent successful publish time.
The change you made is visible in a published channel, not just the Test pane.

instructions: Publish the agent.
Capture the publish confirmation banner or dialog.

learnQueries: Copilot Studio publish agent
Copilot Studio publish channels overview

features.name: Topics & trigger phrases
features.summary: Author custom topics with trigger phrases and understand the system topics you inherit.
features.whyItMatters: Topics are how you pin down conversations that must follow an exact script — compliance disclosures, intake forms, escalation paths — where a generative answer is not acceptable.
concepts: System topics (Greeting, Fallback, Escalate, On Error) already exist; customize them before authoring new ones.
Trigger phrases are training examples, not keyword matches — 5 to 10 varied phrasings beat 30 near-duplicates.
Under generative orchestration the topic **description** matters as much as its trigger phrases.
steps: Open the **Topics** tab and review the system topics.
Select **Add a topic** > **From blank**.
Name the topic and add 5 to 10 varied trigger phrases from real user language.
Add a **Message** node with the response, then branch with a **Question** node if you need input.
Save, then use the **Test** pane to trigger the topic with a phrase you did not train on.
validation: The topic triggers from an untrained but semantically similar phrase.
System topics still handle greeting and fallback correctly.

instructions: Open the Topics tab.
Show both custom and system topics.
Open your new topic's trigger node.
Show the list of trigger phrases.

learnQueries: Copilot Studio topics trigger phrases
Copilot Studio system topics customize

reuseScreenshots.caption: Topics tab — custom and system topics
Trigger phrases for a custom topic

features.name: Entities & variables
features.summary: Capture user input with prebuilt and custom entities, and pass it around with topic and global variables.
features.whyItMatters: Entities turn free text into structured values your tools can actually use, and variables are how a value captured in one topic survives into the next. Without them, every topic starts from zero.
concepts: Prebuilt entities cover common types (date, number, email, city); build custom entities only for domain vocabulary.
Topic variables die at the end of the topic; global variables persist for the conversation.
Slot filling lets the orchestrator fill a variable from something the user already said, skipping the question entirely.
steps: Open your topic and add a **Question** node.
Set **Identify** to a prebuilt entity that matches the value you need.
Create a custom entity under **Settings** > **Entities** for your domain-specific terms and use it in a second Question node.
Save the answer to a variable, then change its scope to **Global**.
Reference the global variable from a different topic and confirm the value carries over.
validation: The prebuilt entity extracts the value from a natural sentence, not just a bare answer.
The custom entity recognizes at least one synonym you defined.
The global variable is readable from a second topic.

instructions: Show a Question node with an entity selected in the Identify dropdown.
Open the variables pane.
Show a variable scoped to Global.

learnQueries: Copilot Studio entities slot filling
Copilot Studio variables global topic scope

reuseScreenshots.caption: Question node using a prebuilt entity

features.name: Adaptive Cards & rich responses
features.summary: Return structured, scannable responses using Adaptive Cards bound to variables.
features.whyItMatters: A wall of prose is unusable on a phone in the field. Adaptive Cards let you show a status, a value, and an action in a layout users can read at a glance — and they render natively in Teams.
concepts: Cards are JSON; bind data with Power Fx expressions rather than string concatenation.
Test card rendering in every channel you publish to — web chat and Teams do not render identically.
Keep cards small: one decision, one or two actions.
steps: In a topic, add a **Send a message** node and switch it to an **Adaptive Card**.
Open the card's JSON editor and lay out the fields you want to show.
Bind each field to a variable using a Power Fx expression.
Preview the card in the authoring canvas.
Test in the **Test** pane, then verify rendering in your target channel.
validation: The card renders with live values, not placeholder text.
Card actions behave correctly in the target channel.

instructions: Show the Adaptive Card JSON editor with your card definition.
Trigger the topic in the Test pane.
Capture the rendered card with real values.

learnQueries: Copilot Studio adaptive cards
Copilot Studio rich response cards Power Fx variables

reuseScreenshots.caption: Adaptive Card preview with bound values

features.name: Power Fx in topics
features.summary: Use Power Fx formulas for conditions, transformations, and lookups inside topic logic.
features.whyItMatters: Power Fx is the deterministic escape hatch. When a value has to be exact — a mapped code, a rounded number, a formatted date — you compute it rather than ask a model to produce it.
concepts: Power Fx runs server-side inside the topic; it is deterministic and cheap compared to a model call.
Use Switch() and record lookups for mapping tables instead of long condition chains.
Formula errors surface at runtime, so exercise every branch in the Test pane.
steps: Add a **Set a variable value** node to a topic.
Switch the value editor to formula mode.
Write a Power Fx expression that transforms or maps an existing variable.
Add a **Condition** node that branches on the computed value.
Test each branch and confirm the computed values are exact.
validation: The computed variable holds the exact expected value for at least three inputs.
Every condition branch has been exercised at least once.

instructions: Show a Set variable node in formula mode with your Power Fx expression.

learnQueries: Copilot Studio Power Fx formulas topics
Copilot Studio use Power Fx variables condition

reuseScreenshots.caption: Power Fx Switch() mapping inside a topic

features.name: SharePoint knowledge
features.summary: Ground the agent in a SharePoint site so it answers from your own documents.
features.whyItMatters: SharePoint is where most organizations already keep policies and procedures. Grounding there gives immediate, permission-trimmed value without moving any content.
concepts: SharePoint knowledge honors the signed-in user's permissions — results are security-trimmed per user.
Indexing is not instant; allow time before judging answer quality.
Narrow the site or document library rather than pointing at an entire tenant — precision beats recall.
steps: Open the **Knowledge** tab and select **Add knowledge**.
Choose **SharePoint** and paste the site or document library URL.
Give the source a clear description so the orchestrator knows when to use it.
Save and wait for indexing to complete.
Ask a question that can only be answered from that site and check the citation.
validation: The answer cites a document from your SharePoint site.
A user without access to the site does not receive the content.

instructions: Show the Add knowledge dialog with SharePoint selected and a URL entered.
Ask a SharePoint-grounded question in the Test pane.
Capture the answer including its citation.

learnQueries: Copilot Studio SharePoint knowledge source
Copilot Studio add knowledge SharePoint permissions

features.name: File uploads & public websites
features.summary: Add uploaded documents and public web sources as additional grounding.
features.whyItMatters: Uploaded files cover the one-off PDF that never made it into SharePoint, and public sites cover authoritative external standards you must not paraphrase from memory.
concepts: Uploaded files are copied into the environment — they follow environment DLP and data residency, not the original file's.
Public website sources are crawled, so deep or JavaScript-heavy pages may not be reachable.
Every source you add competes for orchestrator attention; descriptions are how you break ties.
steps: Open **Knowledge** > **Add knowledge** and choose **Files**.
Upload the document and add a description of what it covers.
Add a second source of type **Public website** and enter the site URL.
Wait for both to finish processing.
Ask one question per source and confirm the citations point to the right source.
validation: A file-grounded question cites the uploaded document.
A web-grounded question cites the public site.

instructions: Show the Knowledge tab listing all configured sources with their status.

learnQueries: Copilot Studio upload files knowledge
Copilot Studio public website knowledge source

features.name: Dataverse knowledge
features.summary: Let the agent answer from structured Dataverse tables in natural language.
features.whyItMatters: Documents answer 'what is the policy'. Dataverse answers 'what is the status of this specific record'. Most real business questions need the second kind.
concepts: Table and column display names are what the model reasons over — cryptic schema names produce bad queries.
Dataverse access is enforced by the caller's security role, so results are trimmed per user.
Restrict the agent to the specific tables and columns it needs rather than the whole environment.
steps: Open **Knowledge** > **Add knowledge** and choose **Dataverse**.
Select the tables the agent should reason over.
Restrict the column list to the fields that matter and confirm the display names are human-readable.
Save and wait for the source to become available.
Ask a record-level question and verify the returned values against the table.
validation: A record-level question returns values that match the Dataverse row.
A user without the security role does not receive the data.

instructions: Show the Dataverse table picker with your selected tables.

learnQueries: Copilot Studio Dataverse knowledge source
Copilot Studio add Dataverse tables agent knowledge

features.name: Grounding & citation tuning
features.summary: Constrain the agent to approved knowledge, control general-knowledge fallback, and verify citations.
features.whyItMatters: An agent that quietly falls back to general model knowledge will eventually invent a policy. Locking grounding to approved sources is the difference between a demo and something legal will sign off on.
concepts: Disabling general knowledge makes the agent say 'I don't know' instead of guessing — that is usually the correct behavior.
Citations are the audit trail; if an answer has no citation, treat it as ungrounded.
Source descriptions steer retrieval more than you expect — rewrite them when routing is wrong.
steps: Open **Settings** > **Generative AI**.
Turn off the option that allows the agent to use its own general knowledge.
Save and ask a question your sources cannot answer.
Confirm the agent declines rather than answering from general knowledge.
Ask three in-scope questions and confirm each answer carries a citation.
validation: An unanswerable question produces a decline, not an invented answer.
Every in-scope answer includes at least one citation.

instructions: Show the Generative AI settings with general knowledge disabled.

learnQueries: Copilot Studio disable general knowledge grounding
Copilot Studio citations knowledge answers

features.name: Connector tools
features.summary: Add a prebuilt Power Platform connector as an agent tool and wire its inputs and outputs.
features.whyItMatters: Connectors are how the agent stops talking and starts doing. Adding one turns a Q&A bot into something that can read live systems of record.
concepts: The tool **description** is what the orchestrator reads to decide when to call it — write it for the model, not for a developer.
Input mapping can be a fixed value, a variable, or a value the model fills at runtime; pick deliberately.
Test the tool in isolation before testing it through conversation, so failures are attributable.
steps: Open the **Tools** tab and select **Add a tool**.
Choose **Connector**, find the connector you need, and pick the specific action.
Create or select the connection and confirm it authenticates.
Write a description that says exactly when the agent should call this tool, then map each input.
Use the tool's built-in test to verify it returns data, then ask a question in the **Test** pane that should invoke it.
validation: The isolated tool test returns real data.
A natural-language question causes the orchestrator to call the tool, visible in the activity map.

instructions: Show the Add a tool flow with a connector action selected.
Show the tool's input mapping configuration.
Run the tool's built-in test.
Capture the returned data.

learnQueries: Copilot Studio connector tool add agent
Copilot Studio tools actions connectors configure inputs

features.name: Custom prompt tools
features.summary: Build a reusable AI prompt in Prompt Builder and expose it to the agent as a tool.
features.whyItMatters: Prompt tools give you a versioned, testable unit of AI behavior — classification, extraction, summarization — that you can reuse across agents and flows instead of burying it in instructions.
concepts: Prompts take typed inputs and can return structured JSON output, which downstream nodes can branch on.
Test with the sample-data panel before wiring the prompt into an agent.
A focused prompt tool usually outperforms adding another paragraph to the agent instructions.
steps: Open **Tools** > **Add a tool** > **Prompt**, or start in Prompt Builder.
Define the prompt's inputs and write the instruction text.
Set the output format — use structured output if a later step needs specific fields.
Test with sample data until the output is stable across several inputs.
Save the prompt as a tool, describe when it should be used, and invoke it from the **Test** pane.
validation: The prompt returns the expected shape for at least three different inputs.
The agent calls the prompt tool for the intended question type.

instructions: Show Prompt Builder with inputs defined and instruction text visible.
Run the prompt test with sample data.
Capture the structured output.

learnQueries: Copilot Studio prompt tool Prompt Builder
Power Platform AI Builder custom prompt structured output

features.name: Custom connectors & OAuth
features.summary: Build a custom Power Platform connector from an OpenAPI spec with OAuth 2.0, then use it as an agent tool.
features.whyItMatters: Line-of-business APIs rarely have a prebuilt connector. A custom connector with OAuth is how you reach them without leaking credentials into the agent.
concepts: Importing an OpenAPI spec generates operations, schemas, and parameters automatically — hand-authoring is a last resort.
OAuth 2.0 with Entra ID lets the connector act as the signed-in user, preserving downstream authorization.
Operation summaries and descriptions become the agent's tool descriptions — write them for the model.
steps: In Power Apps, open **Custom connectors** and create a new connector from an OpenAPI definition.
Configure **Security** for OAuth 2.0 with your Entra ID app registration, scopes, and redirect URL.
Review each operation's summary and description on the **Definition** tab.
Create the connector, then test an operation with a live connection.
Add the connector operation as a tool on your agent and invoke it from the **Test** pane.
validation: The connector test returns a successful response from the live API.
The agent calls the custom connector tool and returns real API data.

instructions: Show the custom connector Security tab configured for OAuth 2.0.
Do not reveal the client secret.
Run an operation on the Test tab.
Capture a successful response.

learnQueries: Power Platform custom connector OpenAPI OAuth Entra ID
Copilot Studio custom connector agent tool

features.name: MCP servers as tools
features.summary: Connect a Model Context Protocol server so its tools appear to the agent automatically.
features.whyItMatters: MCP moves tool definitions out of the agent and into the server. When the server adds a tool, every connected agent gets it — no per-agent rework.
concepts: MCP tools are discovered at connection time, so the agent's tool list changes when the server changes.
The MCP server owns authentication and authorization for the systems behind it.
Tool descriptions come from the server — you inherit their quality, good or bad.
steps: Open **Tools** > **Add a tool** and choose the **Model Context Protocol** option.
Provide the MCP server endpoint and create the connection.
Review the tools the server advertises after discovery completes.
Enable the tools the agent should use and describe when to use them.
Ask a question that requires an MCP tool and confirm the call in the activity map.
validation: Discovered MCP tools are listed on the agent.
The activity map shows an MCP tool call producing the answer.

instructions: Show the discovered MCP tool list after connecting the server.

learnQueries: Copilot Studio Model Context Protocol MCP server tool
Copilot Studio add MCP server agent

reuseScreenshots.caption: Tools discovered from a connected MCP server

features.name: Connected agents
features.summary: Delegate specialized work from a primary agent to child agents with clear role boundaries.
features.whyItMatters: One agent with forty tools routes badly. Splitting by domain keeps each agent's instructions short and its tool list decisive, which measurably improves routing accuracy.
concepts: The parent routes on the child's **description** — overlapping descriptions cause misrouting.
Each child keeps its own instructions, knowledge, and tools; the parent stays thin.
Sharing must be enabled for an agent to be connectable by another agent.
steps: Build or identify a specialist agent and confirm its instructions cover one domain only.
Enable sharing on the specialist so it can be used by other agents.
In the primary agent, open **Agents** and add the specialist as a connected agent.
Write a description that draws a sharp boundary against the primary agent's own scope.
Ask a specialist question and confirm the delegation in the activity map.
validation: A specialist question is delegated to the child agent.
A primary-scope question is NOT delegated.

instructions: Show the connected agent configuration with its description.
Ask a specialist question in the Test pane.
Expand the activity map showing delegation to the child agent.

learnQueries: Copilot Studio connected agents multi-agent
Copilot Studio add agent as tool delegation

features.name: Agent-to-agent (A2A) protocol
features.summary: Connect agents across platforms using the A2A protocol and validate the cross-platform handoff.
features.whyItMatters: A2A is how a Copilot Studio agent reaches a specialist that does not live in Copilot Studio, without either side rewriting its logic as a connector.
concepts: The agent card advertises the remote agent's skills; routing quality depends on it.
Endpoint authentication varies (none, API key, OAuth 2.0) — confirm the mode before wiring.
Cross-platform hops add latency; measure end-to-end, not just the local turn.
steps: Obtain the remote agent's A2A endpoint and its authentication requirements.
In the primary agent, add the remote agent as an A2A connection.
Supply the credentials for the endpoint's authentication mode.
Describe when the primary agent should hand off to the remote agent.
Run a cross-platform question and inspect the request and response in the activity map.
validation: A cross-platform question returns a response produced by the remote agent.
Authentication failures produce a clear, handled error rather than a hang.

instructions: Show the A2A connection configuration.
Mask any secret values.

learnQueries: Copilot Studio agent-to-agent A2A protocol
Copilot Studio connect external agent A2A endpoint

features.name: Agent flows
features.summary: Build a deterministic agent flow and call it from the agent as a tool.
features.whyItMatters: Some work must happen the same way every time — create the ticket, write the row, send the notification. Agent flows give you that determinism while the agent keeps the conversation.
concepts: Flows are triggered by the agent and can return values back into the conversation.
Inputs and outputs form a contract; changing it silently breaks the calling agent.
Flow run history is your audit trail when a user reports a wrong result.
steps: Open **Tools** > **Add a tool** > **New agent flow**.
Define the flow inputs the agent will supply.
Add the action steps that do the work.
Return the outputs the conversation needs, then save and test the flow directly.
Describe the flow tool on the agent and trigger it from the **Test** pane.
validation: A direct flow test succeeds with representative inputs.
The agent triggers the flow and surfaces its output in the conversation.

instructions: Show the agent flow canvas with trigger, actions, and response.
Show a successful flow run with its inputs and outputs.

learnQueries: Copilot Studio agent flows
Copilot Studio create agent flow tool inputs outputs

reuseScreenshots.caption: Agent flow trigger with declared inputs

features.name: Agent flows: prompt nodes
features.summary: Embed AI prompt nodes inside a flow for classification and synthesis with structured outputs.
features.whyItMatters: A prompt node inside a flow lets you branch deterministically on an AI judgement — classify first, then take an exact action — instead of hoping the conversation lands correctly.
concepts: Structured output turns a model response into named fields the next node can branch on.
Always add a fallback branch for unparseable or low-confidence output.
Keep prompt nodes single-purpose so failures are easy to localize.
steps: Open an agent flow and add a **Prompt** node.
Bind the flow input to the prompt's input.
Configure structured output with the fields the next steps need.
Add a **Condition** node that branches on one of those fields.
Add a fallback branch, then test every path.
validation: The prompt node returns parseable structured output.
Each branch, including the fallback, has been exercised.

instructions: Show a prompt node in a flow with structured output configured.

learnQueries: Copilot Studio agent flow prompt node structured output
Power Automate AI prompt action structured output

features.name: Agent flows: async responses
features.summary: Handle long-running work with acknowledgement, completion, timeout, and failure paths.
features.whyItMatters: Users abandon a chat that goes silent for thirty seconds. Async patterns let the agent acknowledge immediately and deliver the result when it is ready.
concepts: Acknowledge the request in the same turn the work starts — silence reads as failure.
Every async path needs an explicit timeout branch, not just a happy path.
Correlate the async result back to the right conversation with an identifier.
steps: Identify the long-running step in your flow and measure its typical duration.
Add an immediate acknowledgement response in the agent before the long step.
Implement the completion path that returns the result to the user.
Add explicit timeout and failure branches with user-visible messaging.
Test the happy path, a timeout, and a hard failure.
validation: The user receives an acknowledgement within a couple of seconds.
Timeout and failure both produce clear messages rather than silence.

instructions: Show the flow with completion, timeout, and failure branches visible.

learnQueries: Copilot Studio agent flow asynchronous long running response
Copilot Studio flow timeout handling agent

features.name: Analytics dashboard
features.summary: Read engagement, resolution, and escalation metrics to find what to fix next.
features.whyItMatters: Analytics is how you replace opinions about agent quality with evidence. The unresolved and escalated buckets are a prioritized backlog you did not have to write.
concepts: Resolution rate without volume context is misleading — always read them together.
Escalation reasons point at missing knowledge or missing tools, not at the model.
Analytics data lags; do not judge a change on the same day you ship it.
steps: Open the **Analytics** tab for the agent.
Set the date range to a period with representative traffic.
Record engagement, resolution, escalation, and abandon rates.
Open the sessions behind the worst-performing bucket and read the transcripts.
Write down the top three concrete improvements the data supports.
validation: You have baseline numbers for the core metrics.
You have three specific, evidence-backed improvements.

instructions: Show the Analytics summary with the date range visible.

learnQueries: Copilot Studio analytics dashboard resolution rate
Copilot Studio analytics overview sessions

features.name: Agent evaluations
features.summary: Build an evaluation test set and run it to baseline quality and catch regressions.
features.whyItMatters: Without an evaluation set, every change is a guess. With one, you can prove a change helped before it reaches users — and prove it did not break anything else.
concepts: Test sets can be auto-generated, imported from CSV, captured from the test canvas, or hand-written; mix all four.
Include adversarial and out-of-scope cases, not just the happy path.
The first run is a baseline, not a grade — its value is comparison over time.
steps: Open the **Evaluations** area for the agent.
Create a test set and add cases using at least two of the available methods.
Include out-of-scope and adversarial cases with their expected refusals.
Run the evaluation and record the baseline results.
Make one improvement, re-run, and compare the two runs.
validation: A baseline evaluation run is saved.
A second run after a change shows a measurable comparison.

instructions: Show the evaluation test set with several cases.
Show the evaluation results with per-case outcomes.

learnQueries: Copilot Studio agent evaluations test set
Copilot Studio evaluate agent quality regression

features.name: Multi-turn conversation tests
features.summary: Script multi-turn regression tests that validate context retention and branching.
features.whyItMatters: Single-turn tests miss the failures users actually hit: the agent forgetting what they said two turns ago, or losing the thread after a clarifying question.
concepts: Test context carryover explicitly — refer back to an earlier answer without repeating it.
Include a topic switch and a switch back to prove state is preserved.
Assert on completion of the task, not just on individual message text.
steps: Write a realistic multi-turn script including a clarifying question.
Add a turn that refers to an earlier answer using a pronoun.
Add a topic switch followed by a return to the original task.
Run the script and record where context was lost.
Fix the causes and re-run the same script.
validation: The agent completes the task across all turns.
The pronoun reference resolves to the right earlier answer.

instructions: Show a multi-turn test script and its run result.

learnQueries: Copilot Studio multi-turn conversation test
Copilot Studio test agent conversation context

features.name: End-user authentication & SSO
features.summary: Configure Entra ID sign-in so the agent acts on behalf of the signed-in user.
features.whyItMatters: Without user authentication, every user sees the same data. With it, SharePoint, Dataverse, and connector results are trimmed to what that specific person is allowed to see.
concepts: Manual Entra ID authentication gives you control over scopes and redirect URLs; Microsoft-managed auth is faster but less flexible.
Scopes decide what downstream systems the agent can reach on the user's behalf — request the minimum.
Changing the authentication mode resets existing connections; plan for re-consent.
steps: Open **Settings** > **Security** > **Authentication**.
Compare the available authentication options and choose the one your scenario requires.
For manual Entra ID, register or reuse an app registration and enter client ID, token URLs, and scopes.
Add the required redirect URL to the app registration.
Save, publish, and validate the sign-in prompt and post-sign-in behavior in a channel.
validation: An unauthenticated user is prompted to sign in.
After sign-in, results are trimmed to that user's permissions.

instructions: Open Settings > Security > Authentication.
Show the authentication options.
Show the manual Entra ID configuration fields.
Do not capture real secrets.

features.name: Content moderation & guardrails
features.summary: Set moderation levels, tighten grounding, and validate refusal behavior against adversarial prompts.
features.whyItMatters: Moderation and explicit scope boundaries are what keep an agent from confidently answering a question it has no business answering. This is usually the gate to production approval.
concepts: Higher moderation reduces risky output but increases false refusals — tune, then measure.
Moderation settings and instruction-level boundaries are complementary, not redundant.
Adversarial testing belongs in your evaluation set so refusals cannot silently regress.
steps: Open **Settings** > **Generative AI** and review the content moderation level.
Set the level appropriate for your audience and save.
Add explicit scope and safety boundaries to the agent instructions.
Run a set of adversarial and out-of-scope prompts.
Record which prompts were refused and add the gaps to your evaluation set.
validation: Adversarial prompts are refused with the documented message.
In-scope prompts still succeed at the chosen moderation level.

instructions: Show the content moderation level control.
Send an adversarial prompt in the Test pane.
Capture the refusal response.

features.name: DLP & environment governance
features.summary: Create tenant DLP policies that classify connectors and scope them to environments.
features.whyItMatters: DLP is the control that stops a maker from wiring a corporate data connector to a public one. It is enforced at the platform, so it survives agents you have never seen.
concepts: Connectors in Business and Non-business groups cannot be combined in the same agent or flow.
Blocked connectors cannot be used at all in the scoped environments.
Policy changes can break existing agents — inventory before you enforce.
steps: Open the Power Platform admin center and go to **Policies** > **Data policies**.
Create a policy and name it for its intent.
Classify connectors into Business, Non-business, and Blocked.
Scope the policy to your target environments.
Save, then confirm a blocked connector is unavailable to a new agent in that environment.
validation: The policy appears in the data policies list scoped to the right environments.
A blocked connector is genuinely unavailable in the scoped environment.

instructions: Show the Data policies list in the Power Platform admin center.
Show connectors grouped into Business, Non-business, and Blocked.

features.name: Solutions & ALM
features.summary: Package the agent into a solution and move it between environments predictably.
features.whyItMatters: Agents built directly in production cannot be reviewed, rolled back, or reproduced. Solutions make an agent a versioned artifact you can promote like any other software.
concepts: Create the agent inside a solution from the start; retrofitting is painful.
Environment variables and connection references keep environment-specific values out of the package.
Managed solutions in downstream environments prevent drift from direct edits.
steps: Create an unmanaged solution in your development environment.
Create or add the agent and its dependencies to that solution.
Replace environment-specific values with environment variables and connection references.
Export the solution as managed.
Import into a test environment, supply the variable values, and validate the agent works.
validation: The managed solution imports without missing-dependency errors.
The imported agent works using the target environment's own values.

instructions: Show the solution contents including the agent and its dependencies.

features.summary: Publish the agent to Microsoft Teams and Microsoft 365 Copilot and validate the end-user experience.
features.whyItMatters: Adoption follows the tools people already have open. Publishing into Teams removes the 'where do I find it' problem that kills most internal agents.
concepts: Teams availability may require admin approval before users can install it.
Rendering differs between Teams and web chat — validate cards in Teams specifically.
The Microsoft 365 Copilot channel surfaces the agent inside Copilot chat rather than as a standalone app.

Turn the channel on and configure availability.
Publish the agent.
Install the agent for yourself and start a conversation in Teams.
Verify text, cards, and any sign-in prompt behave correctly.
validation: The agent is reachable in Teams and answers correctly.

features.name: Embed in a web app (Client SDK)
features.summary: Embed the agent in a custom-branded web page using the Copilot Studio Client SDK with MSAL authentication.
features.whyItMatters: The default web chat is fine for a pilot. A custom embed lets you own branding, layout, and the authentication story — which is what customer-facing deployments actually require.
concepts: The SDK handles the conversation lifecycle; you own rendering and state.
Delegated auth through MSAL.js means the agent runs as the signed-in user.
You must handle adaptive card fallback yourself — the SDK does not render cards for you.
steps: Register an Entra ID application for a single-page application and add your redirect URI.
Install the Copilot Studio client SDK and MSAL.js in your web project.
Acquire a token with MSAL and initialize the client with your agent's connection settings.
Start a conversation, render incoming activities, and handle suggested actions.
Add adaptive card fallback rendering, then style the chat to your brand.
validation: The embedded chat authenticates and exchanges messages with the published agent.
Suggested actions work and cards degrade gracefully.

instructions: Show the branded embedded chat with a live conversation.

features.name: Real-time voice agents
features.summary: Build a real-time voice agent for telephony with turn-taking, hold/resume, and post-call actions.
features.whyItMatters: Voice is where field and customer-facing users actually are. It also punishes latency and ambiguity far more than chat, which forces genuinely better design.
concepts: Voice responses must be short — what reads fine on screen is unbearable spoken.
Barge-in and turn-taking behavior determine whether the call feels natural.
Recording and consent requirements are jurisdictional; confirm before enabling.
steps: Enable the voice channel for the agent.
Rewrite the key responses for spoken delivery and test them aloud.
Configure turn-taking, silence handling, and hold/resume behavior.
Configure post-call actions such as transcript or summary delivery.
Place test calls covering the happy path, a misheard input, and a transfer.
validation: A test call completes the primary task end to end.
Misheard input recovers gracefully instead of looping.

instructions: Show the voice channel configuration with turn-taking settings.

features.name: Computer-using agents
features.summary: Automate a UI-only application with a computer-using agent and govern its execution.
features.whyItMatters: Some systems have no API and never will. Computer use lets an agent drive them the way a person would, which is often the only path to automating legacy workflows.
concepts: Computer use is slower and more brittle than an API — use it when there is no alternative.
Every action needs a verification checkpoint or failures cascade silently.
Run under a dedicated, least-privilege identity and log every session.
steps: Identify a UI-only task and write out each step a person performs.
Create a computer-use tool and describe the task and its success condition.
Add verification checkpoints between steps.
Run the automation and watch the session recording for drift.
Add retries and failure handling, then document the governance model.
validation: The automation completes the task without human intervention.
An injected failure is detected at a checkpoint rather than silently ignored.

instructions: Show the computer-use tool configuration with the task description.

learnQueries: Copilot Studio computer use agent
Copilot Studio computer use tool configure governance

features.name: Work IQ & Microsoft 365 grounding
features.summary: Ground the agent in Microsoft 365 work signals for context-aware answers.
features.whyItMatters: Work IQ brings the user's own working context — files, meetings, communications — into the answer, which is what makes a briefing agent feel personal rather than generic.
concepts: Everything is permission-trimmed to the signed-in user, so end-user authentication is a hard prerequisite.
Answers vary per user by design — evaluate with several personas, not one.
Combine work signals with curated external sources so answers are both personal and authoritative.
steps: Confirm end-user authentication is configured and working.
Add the Microsoft 365 / Work IQ grounding source to the agent.
Describe when the agent should use work context versus curated knowledge.
Test as two different users and compare the answers.
Document what each persona is and is not able to see.
validation: Two different users receive appropriately different, permission-trimmed answers.
No user sees content they cannot access directly in Microsoft 365.

instructions: Show the Microsoft 365 / Work IQ grounding source configured on the agent.

features.name: VS Code agent authoring
features.summary: Clone an agent to VS Code, edit it as source, and republish to the cloud.
features.whyItMatters: Source-based authoring gives you diffs, code review, and branching for agents — the engineering practices that the web canvas cannot provide.
concepts: The cloned agent is YAML on disk; topics, instructions, and tools are all reviewable text.
Publishing from VS Code overwrites the cloud version — coordinate with anyone editing in the browser.
Source authoring pairs naturally with solutions and pipelines for full ALM.

Clone the target agent to a local folder.
Inspect the generated YAML for the agent, its topics, and its tools.
Make a change to instructions or a topic in source.
Publish back to the cloud and verify the change in the Test pane.
validation: The cloned agent's YAML is present locally and readable.
A source-side change appears in the cloud agent after publishing.

features.name: Usage estimation & Copilot Credits
features.summary: Estimate consumption, identify cost drivers, and set rollout guardrails.
features.whyItMatters: Copilot Credits are consumed per interaction and per capability. Knowing your cost curve before rollout is what keeps a successful pilot from becoming an unbudgeted surprise.
concepts: Generative orchestration, tool calls, and larger models each add to per-conversation cost.
Estimate from expected conversations per user per day, not from total headcount.
Set monitoring thresholds before rollout so you notice a spike in hours, not at month end.
steps: Estimate daily active users and conversations per user for your scenario.
Use the usage estimator to model consumption for that volume.
Identify which capabilities dominate the estimate.
Model a lower-cost variant and compare.
Define alert thresholds and a review cadence.
validation: You have a documented estimate with stated assumptions.
You have alert thresholds and an owner for the review cadence.

instructions: Show the usage estimation view with your modeled inputs.
